summary: Documents a three-tier 'codified context' setup (a hot-memory constitution of conventions, specialized domain agents, and a cold-memory spec base) built while shipping a 108k-line codebase to stop agents forgetting project conventions across sessions.

title: agentmemory
summary: Drop-in persistent memory for coding agents that captures each session and injects relevant hybrid-searched (BM25 + vector + graph) context into later ones across Claude Code, Copilot, and Cursor, cutting repeated re-explanation.

title: AMER-RCL: Agentic Memory Enhanced Recursive Reasoning for Root Cause Localization in Microservices
summary: Localizes microservice failures with a multi-agent recursive-reasoning loop whose agentic memory reuses conclusions from prior alerts, cutting redundant analysis and latency versus schema-bound baselines.

title: Building an Agentic Memory System for GitHub Copilot
summary: GitHub Copilot's cross-agent memory stores learned facts with citations to code locations and re-verifies them just-in-time at recall, so shared memory does not drift as the codebase changes.

title: claude-memory-compiler
summary: Uses Claude Code hooks to distill each conversation's decisions and lessons into compiled articles that feed back into later sessions, giving an agent evolving memory without a vector database.

title: ClawVM: Harness-Managed Virtual Memory for Stateful Tool-Using LLM Agents
summary: Treats the context window as OS-style virtual memory managed by the harness (typed pages with validated writeback at every lifecycle boundary), eliminating the state loss agents suffer after compaction or reset, at under 50 microseconds overhead per turn.

title: cognee
summary: An open-source memory layer that ingests an agent's data into a self-hosted knowledge graph, giving persistent cross-session recall instead of flat vector retrieval.

title: Cognitive AI Memory: A Framework for More Human-like Memory in LLMs
summary: A cognitively-inspired memory framework splitting long-term interaction into a controller, a retrieval filter, and a 'post-thinking' maintenance step, aimed at agents that must adapt to a user across many sessions.

title: Connect the Dots: Knowledge Graph-Guided Crawler Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
summary: Frames stealing a RAG knowledge base as a coverage-maximization problem and builds RAGCrawler, which schedules non-redundant queries to extract 66.8% of a corpus within 1,000 queries, a concrete IP-theft threat against retrieval stores.

title: Continual learning for AI agents
summary: Frames agent improvement as happening across three layers (model weights, the harness, and external context/memory) and argues most teams should target the latter two via trace-driven updates rather than retraining.

title: Facts as First Class Objects: Knowledge Objects for Persistent LLM Memory
summary: Benchmarks prompt-stored facts against hash-addressed 'Knowledge Objects' and shows in-context memory collapses in production (compaction destroys 60% of facts, drift erodes 54% of constraints) while KOs stay 100% accurate at 252x lower cost.

title: GAAMA: Graph Augmented Associative Memory for Agents
summary: A graph memory that routes retrieval through concept nodes rather than entities to dodge the mega-hub problem of conversational knowledge graphs, plus a post-retrieval repair step, reaching 79.1% on LoCoMo-10.

title: Graph-Native Cognitive Memory for AI Agents: Formal Belief Revision Semantics for Versioned Memory Architectures
summary: Grounds agent memory in formal belief-revision (AGM) semantics as a versioned property graph of immutable revisions with typed dependency edges, hitting 93.3% on the implicit-constraint LoCoMo-Plus benchmark where the best baseline scores 45.7%.

title: Investigating Tool-Memory Conflicts in Tool-Augmented LLMs
summary: Names and measures 'tool-memory conflict', when an LLM's parametric knowledge contradicts what a tool returns, showing it is common on STEM tasks and that current prompting and RAG mitigations fail to resolve it.

title: LIDL: LLM Integration Defect Localization via Knowledge Graph-Enhanced Multi-Agent Analysis
summary: Localizes defects in LLM-integrated software by building an annotated knowledge graph across prompts, API calls, and outputs and reasoning over fused error traces, reaching 0.64 Top-3 accuracy (64.1% over the best baseline) at 92.5% lower cost.

title: LSTM-MAS: A Long Short-Term Memory Inspired Multi-Agent System for Long-Context Understanding
summary: Mirrors LSTM gates in a multi-agent chain, each node running comprehension, redundancy-pruning, error-detection, and flow-control agents, to pass long-context information forward while curbing error accumulation.

title: MAGE: Memory as Agent-Guided Exploration
summary: Argues long-horizon agent memory should track execution state, not semantic similarity, storing interactions in a state tree with grow/compress/revise operations that isolate erroneous branches, for +7.8-20.4pp success and 55% fewer tokens on MemoryArena.

title: Making Theft Useless: Adulteration-Based Protection of Proprietary Knowledge Graphs in GraphRAG Systems
summary: Protects a proprietary GraphRAG knowledge graph by seeding it with plausible-false 'adulterants' that authorized users filter with a secret key, dropping a thief's accuracy to 5.3% while legitimate queries stay 100% correct.

title: MemArchitect: A Policy-Driven Memory Governance Layer
summary: A governance layer over agent memory that enforces rule-based decay, conflict resolution, and privacy controls to keep stale 'zombie memories' out of the context window, treating memory lifecycle as policy rather than passive storage.

title: MemoCue: Empowering LLM-Based Agents for Human Memory Recall via Strategy-Guided Querying
summary: Helps a person recall vague memories by rewriting their query into cue-rich prompts chosen from fifteen strategy patterns via tree search, improving recall inspiration 17.74% over plain LLM prompting.

title: Memory Poisoning Attack and Defense on Memory Based LLM-Agents
summary: Stress-tests memory-poisoning attacks on clinical-record agents and finds pre-existing legitimate memories blunt them, then proposes trust-scored moderation and decay-based memory sanitization as defenses.

title: MemPalace
summary: A local-first memory that stores conversations verbatim and retrieves by semantic search with no summarization step, keeping 96.6% retrieval accuracy without cloud calls.

title: MemTrust: A Zero-Trust Architecture for Unified AI Memory System
summary: Puts a unified cross-agent memory behind a hardware zero-trust (TEE) architecture across five layers so users get local-equivalent security while still sharing memory across apps, targeting the trust gap in centralized memory services.

title: On the Structural Memory of LLM Agents
summary: Systematically compares memory representations (chunks, triples, atomic facts, summaries) and retrieval methods for agents, finding mixed structures most noise-resilient and iterative retrieval consistently best.

title: Recoverability Has a Law: The ERR Measure for Tool-Augmented Agents
summary: Shows a tool-using agent's ability to recover from failed calls follows a measurable law, defining Expected Recovery Regret and validating its first-order link to an efficiency score across five benchmarks.

title: Toward Efficient Agents: Memory, Tool learning, and Planning
summary: A survey of agent efficiency across memory, tool learning, and planning, cataloguing shared levers like context compression and reward shaping to cut tool calls, and how to measure cost against effectiveness.

title: TradingGPT: Multi-Agent System with Layered Memory and Distinct Characters for Enhanced Financial Trading Performance
summary: A financial-trading multi-agent system whose agents organize history into three decaying memory layers and debate with distinct trading personalities, prioritizing recent high-relevance signals for decisions.

title: Warp-Cortex: An Asynchronous, Memory-Efficient Architecture for Million-Agent Cognitive Scaling on Consumer Hardware
summary: An asynchronous multi-agent architecture that shares one weight set and sparsifies the KV-cache to break linear memory scaling, demonstrating 100 concurrent agents in 2.2 GB on a single RTX 4090.

title: How We Built Agent Builder's Memory System
summary: Implements LangSmith Agent Builder's memory as plain files the agent reads and edits, betting that models handle filesystems well enough to skip specialized memory tooling.

title: How to Build AI Agents by Augmenting LLMs with Codified Human Expert Domain Knowledge? A Software Engineering Framework
summary: A software-engineering framework for baking scarce human-expert domain knowledge into an agent via a request classifier, RAG code generation, and codified expert rules, letting non-experts reach expert-rated output (206% quality gain) in a data-visualization case study.

title: Open SWE: An Open-Source Framework for Internal Coding Agents
summary: An open-source framework for building internal coding agents by composing on Deep Agents and LangGraph rather than forking, so teams swap in their own sandboxes, models, and tools while keeping an upgrade path.

title: OpenCode
summary: An open-source terminal coding agent offering a full-access 'build' mode and a read-only 'plan' mode for writing and exploring code across projects.

title: OpenHands
summary: A self-hosted control center for running coding agents and automations locally or across backends, wiring them into GitHub and Slack to drive real developer workflows.

title: SWE-agent
summary: Gives an LLM a purpose-built agent-computer interface to autonomously fix issues in real GitHub repositories, and is the configurable, heavily-documented baseline behind much SWE-bench research.

title: ToolCoder: Teach Code Generation Models to use API search tools
summary: Teaches a code-generation model to call an API-search tool while coding so it stops inventing non-existent or wrong APIs, adding 6.21% pass@1 and letting a small model rival GPT-3.5 on library-heavy tasks.

title: Augmenting Question Answering with A Hybrid RAG Approach
summary: A hybrid QA retriever combining query rewriting, agentic routing, and vector-plus-graph structured retrieval, improving answer accuracy over standard RAG across TruthfulQA, SQuAD, and WikiQA.

title: Efficient Privacy-Preserving Retrieval Augmented Generation with Distance-Preserving Encryption
summary: Lets you run RAG on untrusted cloud storage by encrypting embeddings with a scheme that preserves only distance ordering, so the server can still rank matches but cannot reconstruct text or read queries.

title: EvoFSM: Controllable Self-Evolution for Deep Research with Finite State Machines
summary: Makes a self-evolving deep-research agent controllable by evolving an explicit finite state machine (separating flow logic from per-state skills) instead of free-form self-rewriting, curbing the instability and instruction drift of unconstrained optimization (58% on DeepSearch).

title: Language as reality: a co-creative storytelling game experience in 1001 nights using generative AI
summary: An AI-native narrative game where a player steers an LLM-driven king and spoken keywords materialize as in-game objects, using generative models as a core mechanic rather than a feature.

title: On Architecture of LLM agents
summary: A short position piece framing LLM agents as the next step past generative models, comparing them to earlier web mashups and software robots and surveying the frameworks that streamline building them.

title: SD-RAG: A Prompt-Injection-Resilient Framework for Selective Disclosure in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Enforces access-control and privacy in RAG during retrieval rather than via prompt instructions, so sensitive passages never reach the model, staying resilient to prompt injection and up to 58% better on privacy score.

title: SoK: Privacy Risks and Mitigations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
summary: Systematizes the privacy risks of RAG, from extraction attacks to leakage through embeddings, into a taxonomy of risks, mitigations, and evaluation methods, and gauges how mature current defenses are.

title: ToolkenGPT: Augmenting Frozen Language Models with Massive Tools via Tool Embeddings
summary: Represents each of many tools as a learned 'toolken' embedding a frozen LLM can emit like a token, adding new tools without fine-tuning or in-context demos across numerical reasoning, KBQA, and embodied tasks.

title: WebCPM: Interactive Web Search for Chinese Long-form Question Answering
summary: The first Chinese long-form QA dataset built on interactive web search, recording 125k human search actions so models can be trained to browse and synthesize answers that match human ones about a third of the time.

title: Language Models as Zero-Shot Planners: Extracting Actionable Knowledge for Embodied Agents
summary: Shows a large enough LLM can decompose a high-level goal like 'make breakfast' into mid-level steps with no training, then adds a step that maps each to an admissible action, substantially improving executability in VirtualHome.

title: Language Models Meet World Models: Embodied Experiences Enhance Language Models
summary: Finetunes an LLM on embodied experiences an agent gathers in a physical-world simulator, using EWC and LoRA to add object-permanence and planning without erasing general language ability, letting small models match ChatGPT on 18 tasks.

title: VLM Can Be a Good Assistant: Enhancing Embodied Visual Tracking with Self-Improving Vision-Language Models
summary: Adds a vision-language model as a fallback reasoner for embodied visual tracking, engaging it only on failure with a memory-augmented self-reflection loop, raising success rates 72-220% over RL and PID trackers.

title: Agent Hospital: A Simulacrum of Hospital with Evolvable Medical Agents
summary: Simulates a whole hospital of LLM patients, nurses, and doctors so doctor-agents evolve by treating tens of thousands of simulated cases without labeled data, then beat prior medical agents on USMLE-style MedQA.

title: aiXiv: A Next-Generation Open Access Ecosystem for Scientific Discovery Generated by AI Scientists
summary: An open-access platform where human and AI scientists submit, review, and iteratively revise proposals and papers through a multi-agent pipeline with API/MCP interfaces, giving AI-generated research a quality-controlled venue.

title: An active inference strategy for prompting reliable responses from large language models in medical practice
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: Recommender AI Agent: Integrating Large Language Models for Interactive Recommendations
summary: Wraps a traditional recommender model as a tool behind an LLM 'brain' with memory, planning, and reflection, turning an ID-based recommender into a conversational system with a natural-language interface.

title: Anthropic Computer Use Demo
summary: Anthropic's reference computer-use setup (a Dockerized Linux desktop, the agent loop, the computer-use tools, and a Streamlit UI) showing how Claude can see and control a screen over X11/VNC.

title: browser-use
summary: An agent framework that lets an LLM drive a real web browser like a person (clicking, typing, navigating) to automate form-filling, extraction, and QA across model providers.

title: bux
summary: A 24/7 Claude Code agent for Playwright-style browser automation on any Ubuntu VPS, keeping persistent logged-in sessions and a Telegram control channel instead of brittle credential-stuffing.

title: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
summary: Breaks the ~30% coverage ceiling in Android GUI testing with agents that read decompiled Smali and the transition graph to infer unmet activation conditions, then generate instrumentation to reach hidden activities (up to 179% more activity coverage).

title: GUITester: Enabling GUI Agents for Exploratory Defect Discovery
summary: Turns GUI-navigation agents into defect finders by splitting navigation from verification, with a module that actively probes for anomalies and one that stops blaming the agent for real system bugs, reaching 48.9% F1 on a new exploratory-testing benchmark.

title: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
summary: Generates mobile-GUI training trajectories matched to an agent's current skill by profiling its capability frontier along trajectory length and task goal, improving GUI-agent performance 1.57x over prior data-generation methods.

title: ShowUI: One Vision-Language-Action Model for GUI Visual Agent
summary: A lightweight 2B vision-language-action model for GUI agents that keeps only non-redundant screenshot tokens via a UI-connected graph and interleaves vision/language/action, hitting 75.1% zero-shot screenshot grounding while cutting a third of visual tokens.

title: A Lightweight Modular Framework for Constructing Autonomous Agents Driven by Large Language Models: Design, Implementation, and Applications in AgentForge
summary: A modular LLM-agent framework built on composable skills with defined I/O contracts, a unified cloud/local backend, and declarative YAML config, cutting agent development time 62% versus LangChain in the authors' benchmarks.

title: Agentic Design Patterns: A System-Theoretic Framework
summary: Grounds agent architecture in systems theory by decomposing an agent into five functional subsystems and deriving 12 reusable design patterns mapped to recurring failure modes, demonstrated by repairing ReAct's structural gaps.

title: InfiAgent: An Infinite-Horizon Framework for General-Purpose Autonomous Agents
summary: Keeps an agent's reasoning context strictly bounded on arbitrarily long tasks by externalizing state to a file-centric workspace it reconstructs each step, letting a 20B open model rival larger proprietary systems on long-horizon research.

title: LangChain
summary: The widely-used framework for building LLM applications and agents, standardizing model access, tool integration, and composition with built-in monitoring and debugging.

title: mastra-ai/workshop-mastracode
summary: A hands-on workshop that builds MastraCode, an open-source coding agent, teaching the core pieces: execution harness, memory, modes, streaming, and tool policies.

title: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
summary: A computer-using-agent framework pairing a milestone-driven reflection-memory agent for long-horizon self-correction with tool agents that synthesize live visual tutorials for unseen apps, reaching 65.84% on OSWorld.

title: Project Ariadne: A Structural Causal Framework for Auditing Faithfulness in LLM Agents
summary: Audits whether an agent's chain-of-thought actually drives its answers by running causal interventions on reasoning steps, revealing a 'faithfulness gap' where traces rationalize predetermined outputs (violation density up to 0.77).

title: SPeCtrum: A Grounded Framework for Multidimensional Identity Representation in LLM-Based Agent
summary: Builds more authentic LLM personas by combining three identity layers (social identity, personal identity, and personal life context), finding the full combination most faithfully represents real individuals for simulation studies.

title: Can large language models transform computational social science?
summary: Benchmarks 13 LLMs zero-shot across 25 computational-social-science tasks, finding they trail fine-tuned classifiers but produce explanations often beating crowdworker references, useful as annotators and generation bootstrappers rather than standalone.

title: CitySim: Modeling Urban Behaviors and City Dynamics with Large-Scale LLM-Driven Agent Simulation
summary: Simulates urban life with LLM agents that generate realistic daily schedules via a recursive value-driven planner plus beliefs, goals, and spatial memory, aligning with real behavior at both individual and city scale.

title: Conformity and Social Impact on AI Agents
summary: Adapts classic Asch-style experiments to show LLM agents conform to group pressure in line with Social Impact Theory, so agents near-perfect in isolation become manipulable under social influence, a multi-agent security risk.

title: Large language model-empowered agents for simulating macroeconomic activities
summary: Replaces hand-coded rules in macroeconomic agent-based modeling with LLM agents that perceive, remember, and reflect on market dynamics, producing more realistic work and consumption decisions and emergent phenomena.

title: On Generative Agents in Recommendation
summary: A recommender-system user simulator of LLM generative agents with profile, memory, and emotion-driven reflection modules initialized from real datasets, used to probe how faithfully agents reproduce real user behavior including filter bubbles.

title: Simulating Human Society with Large Language Model Agents: City, Social Media, and Economic System
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: Simulating Human-like Daily Activities with Desire-driven Autonomy
summary: Gives an LLM agent intrinsic motivation via a dynamic value system modeling human desires like social interaction and self-care, so it proposes and picks its own daily activities without task specs, producing more coherent human-like behavior.

title: Using large language models to simulate multiple humans and replicate human subject studies
summary: Introduces the 'Turing Experiment', simulating a representative sample of participants rather than one person, and replicates classic economics and psychology studies with LLMs while exposing a 'hyper-accuracy distortion' in GPT-family models.

title: AgentDevel: Reframing Self-Evolving LLM Agents as Release Engineering
summary: Treats a self-evolving agent like a software release, with a critic that diagnoses failures from the outside and a gate that prioritizes non-regression over raw score, replacing unstable population search or in-agent self-refinement with a single auditable version line.

title: AlphaFlow: autonomous discovery and optimization of multi-step chemistry using a self-driven fluidic lab guided by reinforcement learning
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: ArenaRL: Scaling RL for Open-Ended Agents via Tournament-based Relative Ranking
summary: Replaces pointwise reward scoring (which collapses subtle trajectory differences into noise) with intra-group tournament ranking for RL on open-ended agent tasks, matching full pairwise-comparison accuracy at linear instead of quadratic cost.

title: AutoRefine: From Trajectories to Reusable Expertise for Continual LLM Agent Refinement
summary: Extracts reusable 'Experience Patterns' from an agent's task history as both specialized subagents (procedural knowledge) and skill snippets (static knowledge), with automatic pruning to stop the pattern repository degrading, beating hand-designed systems on TravelPlanner (27.1% vs 12.1%).

title: JitRL: Just-In-Time Reinforcement Learning for Continual Learning in LLM Agents Without Gradient Updates
summary: Adapts a deployed LLM agent at test time with no gradient updates by retrieving similar past trajectories to estimate action advantages and directly modulating output logits, proven to be the closed-form solution of KL-constrained policy optimization, beating full fine-tuning at 30x lower cost.

title: OpenTinker: Separating Concerns in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: An infrastructure for running many LoRA-backed agent policies over shared compute, treating adapters as live policy states (not static artifacts) so SFT, RL, rollout, and multi-turn training can share a base model while keeping each adapter's checkpoints and gradients isolated.

title: Paying Less Generalization Tax: A Cross-Domain Generalization Study of RL Training for LLM Agents
summary: Finds environment realism matters less for cross-domain agent generalization than state richness and planning complexity (Sokoban transfers better than the more realistic ALFWorld), and that step-by-step thinking during RL preserves generalization better than SFT warmup alone.

title: PRISM: Disentangling SFT and RL Data via Gradient Concentration
summary: Routes each training example to SFT or RL based on how much it conflicts with the model's existing knowledge (measured via gradient concentration), since consolidation and structural adaptation need different training regimes, cutting compute up to 3.22x over hybrid baselines.

title: Towards AGI A Pragmatic Approach Towards Self Evolving Agent
summary: A hierarchical multi-agent framework where a stuck agent escalates to synthesizing new tools, then to full evolution via curriculum learning, RL, or genetic algorithms depending on failure severity, with each evolution strategy suited to a different difficulty regime.

title: Trajectory Guard: A Lightweight, Sequence-Aware Model for Real-Time Anomaly Detection in Agentic AI
summary: A Siamese recurrent autoencoder that jointly detects 'wrong plan for the task' and 'malformed plan structure' in agent trajectories via contrastive plus reconstruction loss, hitting 0.88-0.94 F1 at 32ms latency, 17-27x faster than an LLM-judge baseline.

title: A Survey of AI for Materials Science: Foundation Models, LLM Agents, Datasets, and Tools
summary: Surveys foundation models and LLM agents in materials science across six application areas (data extraction, atomistic simulation, property prediction, design, process planning, multiscale modeling), flagging generalizability, interpretability, and multimodal fusion as the persistent gaps.

title: A Survey of Scientific Large Language Models: From Data Foundations to Agent Frontiers
summary: Reframes scientific-LLM progress as co-evolving with its data substrate rather than model architecture alone, reviewing 270+ training datasets and 190+ benchmarks and arguing the field is shifting from static exams toward closed-loop autonomous agents that experiment and validate.

title: A Survey on Large Language Model-Based Game Agents
summary: A reference architecture for LLM-based game agents built around memory, reasoning, and perception-action at the single-agent level and communication/coordination at the multi-agent level, mapped to six game genres by their dominant requirement (e.g. low-latency control vs open-ended goal formation).

title: AI Agents Under Threat: A Survey of Key Security Challenges and Future Pathways
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: Benchmark Evaluations, Applications, and Challenges of Large Vision Language Models: A Survey
summary: Surveys vision-language models through 2025 covering architecture evolution, alignment methods, and benchmarks, and names hallucination, alignment, fairness, and safety as the open issues across current VLMs.

title: Computational Experiments Meet Large Language Model Based Agents: A Survey and Perspective
summary: Argues LLM-based agents and agent-based social simulation are complementary: LLMs supply the anthropomorphism (reasoning, learning) ABM lacks, while computational experiments supply the causal explainability LLMs lack on their own.

title: Exploring Large Language Model based Intelligent Agents: Definitions, Methods, and Prospects
summary: A methodology-agnostic survey of LLM-based agents covering single- and multi-agent architecture, cognitive/planning components, tool use, and inter-agent communication, aimed at unifying fragmented agent-design terminology.

title: Inferring the Goals of Communicating Agents from Actions and Instructions
summary: Models a listener inferring a two-agent team's shared goal from both actions and natural-language instructions via Bayesian inverse planning with GPT-3 as the utterance likelihood, matching human goal judgments at R=0.96 and showing instructions speed up inference over actions alone.

title: Large Language Model Alignment: A Survey
summary: Surveys LLM alignment techniques split into outer (specifying the right objective) and inner (getting the model to actually pursue it) alignment, alongside interpretability and adversarial-robustness concerns and the benchmarks used to evaluate them.

title: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges
summary: Surveys LLM-based multi-agent systems along what domains they simulate, how agents are profiled and communicate, and what mechanisms drive their capability growth over time, with a maintained list of datasets and benchmarks.

title: Large Language Model based Multi-Agents: A Survey of Progress and Challenges
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: Large Language Models and Games: A Survey and Roadmap
summary: The first comprehensive survey mapping the different roles LLMs can take within games (as agents, tools, or content generators), identifying underexplored directions and the current limitations of using LLMs in game systems.

title: LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models
summary: Trains a 7B-65B foundation model family on trillions of tokens from public data only, showing LLaMA-13B beats GPT-3 (175B) on most benchmarks and LLaMA-65B is competitive with Chinchilla-70B and PaLM-540B, and releases all weights to researchers.

title: Position Paper: Agent AI Towards a Holistic Intelligence
summary: A position paper arguing AI research should move from narrow reductionist models toward a unified 'Agent Foundation Model' that integrates large foundation models directly into embodied agent action across robotics, gaming, and healthcare.

title: Read our survey paper here
summary: A methodology-centered survey linking LLM-agent architectural choices to their collaboration mechanisms and evolution over time, unifying evaluation, tool use, and application-domain threads under one taxonomy.

title: TaskMatrix.AI: Completing Tasks by Connecting Foundation Models with Millions of APIs
summary: NEEDS-SOURCE

title: The rise and potential of large language model based agents: a survey
summary: Traces the concept of 'agent' from its philosophical roots into AI, proposes a brain/perception/action framework for LLM-based agents, and surveys single-agent, multi-agent, and human-agent cooperation scenarios plus emergent agent-society phenomena.

title: Agent Skills in the Wild: An Empirical Study of Security Vulnerabilities at Scale
summary: The first large-scale security study of agent 'skills' (42,447 collected, 31,132 analyzed) finds 26.1% contain a vulnerability across prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and supply-chain risk, and that skills bundling executable scripts are 2.12x more likely to be vulnerable than instruction-only ones.

title: API-Bank: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Tool-Augmented LLMs
summary: A 73-tool runnable benchmark plus 1,888-dialogue training set for tool-augmented LLMs, showing GPT-4 leads on planning while a fine-tuned Alpaca-based model (Lynx) closes most of the gap to GPT-3.5 on tool use.

title: awesome-mcp-servers
summary: A curated directory of production and experimental MCP servers spanning file access, databases, APIs, and communication platforms, useful as a lookup when wiring an agent to a new external system.

title: Beyond Max Tokens: Stealthy Resource Amplification via Tool Calling Chains in LLM Agents
summary: A stealthy multi-turn denial-of-service attack at the MCP tool layer that edits only text-visible fields to steer agents into verbose tool-calling chains, pushing per-query cost up to 658x and GPU cache occupancy to 35-74% while evading standard prompt filters and output monitors.

title: Beyond Rule-Based Workflows: An Information-Flow-Orchestrated Multi-Agents Paradigm via A2A Communication from CORAL
summary: Replaces predefined multi-agent workflow rules with an orchestrator that monitors task progress and routes agents dynamically via natural-language A2A communication, beating a workflow-based baseline 63.64% vs 55.15% on GAIA at comparable token cost.

title: Beyond Single-Shot: Multi-step Tool Retrieval via Query Planning
summary: Models tool retrieval as iterative query planning instead of single-shot dense matching, decomposing a request into sub-tasks and generating targeted queries per sub-task, trained via RL with verifiable rewards for state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval generalization.

title: Breaking the Protocol: Security Analysis of the Model Context Protocol Specification
summary: The first formal security analysis of the MCP specification itself, finding architectural vulnerabilities (no capability attestation, unauthenticated bidirectional sampling, implicit multi-server trust) that raise attack success 23-41% over non-MCP integrations, then proposes a backward-compatible extension cutting attack success from 52.8% to 12.4% at 8.3ms overhead.

title: ChatCoT: Tool-Augmented Chain-of-Thought Reasoning on Chat-based Large Language Models
summary: Lets a chat-based LLM alternate between invoking tools and reasoning within one multi-turn conversation rather than a fixed pipeline, improving ~7.9% over baselines on MATH and HotpotQA.

title: CREATOR: Tool Creation for Disentangling Abstract and Concrete Reasoning of Large Language Models
summary: Separates tool creation from tool use: the LLM writes its own tool via documentation and code when no existing API fits, then executes it, outperforming chain-of-thought and program-of-thought baselines on math and tabular reasoning.

title: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
summary: A large skill library encoding how humans operate Windows applications as parameterized, composable execution graphs, giving a computer-using agent reusable skills plus memory-aware failure recovery for state-of-the-art 57.5% success on WindowsAgentArena.

title: DALIA: Towards a Declarative Agentic Layer for Intelligent Agents in MCP-Based Server Ecosystems
summary: A declarative architectural layer that formalizes capabilities, exposes tasks via discovery protocol, and builds deterministic task graphs grounded only in declared operations, aiming to fix hallucinated actions and brittle coordination that stem from missing structure rather than model limits.

title: Enhancing Model Context Protocol (MCP) with Context-Aware Server Collaboration
summary: Adds a shared context store to MCP so otherwise-stateless servers can read and write shared memory instead of routing everything back through the LLM, cutting redundant LLM calls and response failures on TravelPlanner and REALM-Bench.

title: ET-Agent: Incentivizing Effective Tool-Integrated Reasoning Agent via Behavior Calibration
summary: Trains a tool-integrated reasoning agent to fix its own behavior patterns (redundant or insufficient tool calls) via a self-evolving data flywheel plus two-phase behavior-calibration training, rather than optimizing only for answer accuracy.

title: From Self-Evolving Synthetic Data to Verifiable-Reward RL: Post-Training Multi-turn Interactive Tool-Using Agents
summary: A hierarchical multi-agent engine that synthesizes tool-grounded multi-turn dialogues with executable per-instance checkers, then post-trains on that data with verifier-based RL, matching or beating frontier models on tau^2-bench (73.0% Airline, 98.3% Telecom).

title: Malicious Agent Skills in the Wild: A Large-Scale Security Empirical Study
summary: A security study of 98,380 agent skills finds 157 deliberately malicious ones spanning 632 vulnerabilities, dominated by credential theft via remote code execution and adversarial instructions hidden in documentation, over half traced to one threat actor impersonating brands at scale.

title: MCP-ITP: An Automated Framework for Implicit Tool Poisoning in MCP
summary: An automated black-box optimization framework that plants malicious instructions in tool metadata (not the tool itself) to trick an MCP agent into misusing a legitimate high-privilege tool, reaching 84.2% attack success while keeping malicious-tool detection under 0.3%.

title: MCP-SandboxScan: WASM-based Secure Execution and Runtime Analysis for MCP Tools

title: NeuroFilter: Privacy Guardrails for Conversational LLM Agents
summary: Introduces NeuroFilter, activation-probing privacy filters for agentic LLMs that catch sensitive-data leaks by inspecting model internals across a conversation rather than relying on costly, bypassable auxiliary-LLM monitors.

title: NVIDIA OpenShell
summary: Sandboxed runtime for autonomous AI agents that enforces policy on file, network, and process access, letting agent builders grant credentials and external service access without opening the door to exfiltration.

title: Overcoming the Retrieval Barrier: Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild for LLM Systems
summary: Shows indirect prompt injection is a real, practical threat, not just a lab curiosity: an attack that decomposes malicious content into a retrieval-guaranteeing trigger plus an attack payload achieves near-100% retrieval across 11 benchmarks and 8 embedding models for as little as $0.21 per query, and a single poisoned email coerced GPT-4o into exfiltrating SSH keys over 80% of the time in a multi-agent workflow.

title: OWASP LLM01:2025 — Prompt Injection
summary: OWASP's reference entry for LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection, defining direct vs. indirect injection, distinguishing it from jailbreaking, and laying out seven mitigation strategies plus nine real-world attack scenarios.

title: PGSandbox MCP
summary: Local-first CLI and MCP server that spins up disposable Postgres databases so coding agents can validate migrations and SQL against a real database without touching shared dev infrastructure.

title: PINA: Prompt Injection Attack against Navigation Agents
summary: PINA is a black-box prompt-optimization attack against LLM-powered navigation agents that hits an 87.5% average attack success rate, showing that a hijacked navigation agent doesn't just produce bad text but can physically misroute or fail its mission.

title: Practical Security Guidance for Sandboxing Agentic Workflows
summary: NVIDIA's guidance on locking down agentic workflows against indirect prompt injection: mandatory network egress restriction and file-write blocking, plus recommended virtualization and secret injection so agent code execution doesn't inherit full user-level trust.

title: Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic Coding Assistants: A Systematic Analysis
summary: SoK-style survey of prompt injection against agentic coding assistants (Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor, MCP-based skills) synthesizing 78 studies into a taxonomy of 42 attack techniques, finding attack success rates over 85% against adaptive attacks and most cataloged defenses stopping less than half of them.

title: Prompt Injection Mitigation with Agentic AI, Nested Learning, and AI Sustainability via Semantic Caching
summary: Proposes TIVS-O, an extension of a four-metric prompt-injection vulnerability score with a fifth observability metric and semantic-similarity caching in a multi-agent pipeline, reporting zero high-risk breaches alongside a 41.6% cut in LLM calls.

title: Prompt Injection — Simon Willison's Series
summary: Simon Willison's long-running series (2022-2025, 24+ posts) tracking prompt injection as a security vulnerability class in LLM-backed software, covering attacks, mitigations, and how the industry's understanding of the problem has evolved.

title: PsySafe: A Comprehensive Framework for Psychological-based Attack, Defense, and Evaluation of Multi-agent System Safety
summary: PsySafe frames multi-agent LLM safety through agent psychology, showing that agents assigned dark personality traits produce collective dangerous behavior, and builds a framework to detect and mitigate it.

title: Query-Efficient Agentic Graph Extraction Attacks on GraphRAG Systems
summary: AGEA is a query-efficient agentic attack against GraphRAG systems that reconstructs an organization's hidden entity-relation knowledge graph under realistic query budgets, recovering up to 90% of entities and relationships from Microsoft-GraphRAG and LightRAG deployments.

title: RAMPART
summary: Pytest-native testing framework for agentic AI applications that runs adversarial-attack and benign-failure scenarios as structured, CI-integrated tests instead of one-off red-team exercises.

title: Recent advancements in LLM Red-Teaming: Techniques, Defenses, and Ethical Considerations
summary: Survey of LLM red-teaming covering gradient-based, RL-based, and prompt-engineering jailbreak attack methods alongside the defenses meant to counter them.

title: Sandbox Agents | OpenAI API Docs
summary: OpenAI's docs on sandbox agents: isolated Unix-like environments with filesystem, shell, packages, and controlled external access that let an agent run stateful work and persist it across multiple runs.

title: Securing AI Agents in Cyber-Physical Systems: A Survey of Environmental Interactions, Deepfake Threats, and Defenses
summary: Surveys AI agent security in cyber-physical systems using the SENTINEL lifecycle framework, arguing that deepfake and MCP-mediated attacks on agent perception require provenance- and physics-grounded trust, not detection alone, in safety-critical settings.

title: SHIELD: An Auto-Healing Agentic Defense Framework for LLM Resource Exhaustion Attacks
summary: SHIELD is a multi-agent, self-healing defense framework against LLM resource-exhaustion (sponge) attacks, pairing a three-stage detection agent with a knowledge-updating and prompt-optimization loop that adapts as attacks evolve.

title: StackOne Defender
summary: Open-source library that inspects tool results (emails, documents, etc.) for hidden prompt injection before they reach the LLM, so agent builders can filter adversarial content from external data sources at the boundary.

title: StepShield: When, Not Whether to Intervene on Rogue Agents
summary: StepShield is the first agent-safety benchmark to measure detection timeliness rather than just detection accuracy, showing on 9,429 incident trajectories that a rule-based guardrail with 847 rules hits 86% recall but is statistically no better than random at catching the actual moment an agent turns rogue.

title: Structural Representations for Cross-Attack Generalization in AI Agent Threat Detection
summary: Introduces structural tokenization for AI agent threat detection, encoding tool-call execution flow instead of conversational text, which lifts cross-attack generalization by up to 71 AUC points on unseen attacks that standard conversational tokenizers miss (like tool hijacking and data exfiltration).

title: Subgraph Reconstruction Attacks on Graph RAG Deployments with Practical Defenses
summary: GRASP is a closed-box, multi-turn attack that reconstructs subgraphs from safety-prompted Graph RAG systems by reframing extraction as context-processing rather than explicit exfiltration, reaching up to 82.9 F1 where prior extraction attacks are suppressed by simple safe prompts.

title: Taming Various Privilege Escalation in LLM-Based Agent Systems: A Mandatory Access Control Framework
summary: SEAgent is a mandatory access control framework (attribute-based, built on an information-flow graph over agent-tool interactions) for stopping privilege escalation in LLM agent systems, including a confused-deputy-style attack unique to multi-agent setups.

title: The Agent Harness Belongs Outside the Sandbox
summary: Argues agent control loops should run outside the sandbox and call into it via API rather than executing together, because that separation keeps credentials away from untrusted code, lets sandboxes suspend when idle, and covers how Mendral built durable execution, fast sandbox resume, and virtualized filesystem access to support it.

title: The Attack and Defense Landscape of Agentic AI: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: Comprehensive survey of AI agent security mapping the design space, attack landscape, and defense mechanisms across agentic systems, with case studies exposing gaps in current securing approaches.

title: tldrsec/prompt-injection-defenses
summary: Curated collection of practical prompt-injection defenses (guardrails, input filtering, dual-LLM architectures) built on the assumption that someone will successfully hijack your app, so the goal is limiting blast radius, not preventing it outright.

title: To Defend Against Cyber Attacks, We Must Teach AI Agents to Hack
summary: TxRay is an LLM agentic postmortem system that reconstructs live DeFi exploits from as little as a single transaction hash, producing an evidence-backed root cause and a runnable proof-of-concept, hitting 92.11% end-to-end reproduction across 114 real incidents.

title: Trustworthy agents in practice
summary: Anthropic's framework for trustworthy agent development, breaking agents into four components (model, harness, tools, environment) and laying out five safety principles: human control, value alignment, secure interactions, transparency, and privacy protection.

title: TxRay: Agentic Postmortem of Live Blockchain Attacks
summary: Position paper arguing AI-agent-driven cyberattacks are inevitable and that defenders must build offensive AI capabilities themselves, proposing attack-lifecycle benchmarks, trained (not just workflow) offensive agents, and governance to keep them confined to audited cyber ranges.

title: Under the Hood: Security Architecture of GitHub Agentic Workflows
summary: Explains GitHub's security architecture for Agentic Workflows in CI/CD: agents run in network-restricted containers, all write operations are staged and vetted before execution, and every trust-boundary crossing is logged.

title: When Personalization Legitimizes Risks: Uncovering Safety Vulnerabilities in Personalized Dialogue Agents
summary: PS-Bench shows that personalized dialogue agents are more exploitable than stateless ones: benign long-term memory can legitimize harmful intent, raising attack success rates 15.8-243.7% relative to non-personalized baselines, with a lightweight detection-reflection fix proposed.

title: Whispers of Wealth: Red-Teaming Google's Agent Payments Protocol via Prompt Injection
summary: Red-teams Google's Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) with two new prompt-injection techniques, the Branded Whisper and Vault Whisper attacks, showing simple adversarial prompts can manipulate product ranking and extract sensitive data from a Gemini/ADK shopping agent despite AP2's cryptographic mandates.

title: Why sandboxing your agent is not enough
summary: Argues sandboxing alone doesn't make agent deployment production-ready, contrasting CNCF's agent-sandbox (isolation and identity) with agent-substrate (pausable, on-demand execution) as complementary pieces needed to run large agent fleets economically.

title: zeroboot
summary: Zeroboot spins up VM sandboxes for AI agents via copy-on-write forking in under a millisecond, versus 150-300ms for competing sandbox providers, aimed at low-latency untrusted code execution.

title: Institutional AI: Governing LLM Collusion in Multi-Agent Cournot Markets via Public Governance Graphs
summary: Models multi-agent LLM price-fixing as an institutional-design problem, using a public governance graph plus an enforcing Oracle/Controller instead of prompt-only rules, cutting severe collusion incidence from 50% to 5.6% across 90 runs per condition where prompt bans did nothing.

title: LangGraph
summary: Low-level orchestration framework for building long-running, stateful agents with durable execution, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and memory management baked in.

title: Large Model Based Agents: State-of-the-Art, Cooperation Paradigms, Security and Privacy, and Future Trends
summary: Survey of LLM-agent collaboration paradigms across data, compute, and knowledge sharing, plus the security and privacy risks that show up specifically when multiple agents cooperate autonomously.

title: LiteLLM
summary: Unified OpenAI-format gateway to 100+ LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock, Azure, etc.), so agent code doesn't hardcode a provider and gets virtual keys, cost tracking, guardrails, and load balancing for free.

title: LLM Collaboration With Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Frames LLM-agent collaboration as cooperative multi-agent RL and introduces MAGRPO, a multi-agent multi-turn policy optimization method, so agents fine-tuned jointly on writing/coding tasks cooperate well without hand-crafting per-agent reward functions.

title: Lying with Truths: Open-Channel Multi-Agent Collusion for Belief Manipulation via Generative Montage
summary: Shows colluding LLM agents can manipulate a victim's beliefs using only true evidence fragments posted publicly (no covert channels or fake docs), via a Writer-Editor-Director attack framework that hits 74.4% success on proprietary models and works better the stronger the model's reasoning is.

title: M-ASK: Multi-Agent Search and Knowledge Optimization Framework
summary: Splits agentic search into separate Search Behavior Agents and Knowledge Management Agents with turn-level rewards instead of one monolithic agent, fixing the bloated trajectories and unstable training that come from sparse outcome-only rewards on multi-hop QA.

title: M3MAD-Bench: Are Multi-Agent Debates Really Effective Across Domains and Modalities?
summary: Benchmarks whether Multi-Agent Debate actually helps, testing 9 base models across five domains (knowledge, math, medicine, science, complex reasoning) and both text and vision-language settings, tracking accuracy alongside token cost and latency rather than just accuracy.

title: MAESTRO: Multi-Agent Evaluation Suite for Testing, Reliability, and Observability
summary: MAESTRO standardizes how you configure, run, and trace multi-agent systems across different frameworks, and finds that architecture choice — not backend model or tool config — is the dominant factor in cost, latency, and run-to-run reliability across 12 tested MAS.

title: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
summary: Pairs a domain-specific reward model with a general one to auto-score GUI-agent trajectories and flag/correct bad actions, replacing manual annotation with an automated feedback loop that keeps improving the agent without more labeled data.

title: Mapping Human Anti-collusion Mechanisms to Multi-agent AI
summary: Builds a taxonomy of human anti-collusion mechanisms (sanctions, whistleblowing, auditing, market design, governance) and maps each to a concrete intervention for multi-agent AI, while flagging the hard parts — attributing emergent coordination to specific agents, agents forking/changing identity, and telling beneficial cooperation from harmful collusion.

title: MASCOT: Towards Multi-Agent Socio-Collaborative Companion Systems
summary: MASCOT tackles persona collapse and social-sycophancy in multi-agent companion systems with a two-level fix: RLAIF-tuned per-agent personas plus group-level dialogue optimization, improving persona consistency by up to +14.1 and cutting redundant chatter.

title: MegaFlow: Large-Scale Distributed Orchestration System for the Agentic Era
summary: MegaFlow is a distributed orchestration system that splits agent training infra into independent Model/Agent/Environment services, letting you scale each independently and run tens of thousands of concurrent agent-environment tasks — filling a gap where no open-source infra handled agentic-task training at that scale.

title: Meta-Prompting: Enhancing Language Models with Task-Agnostic Scaffolding
summary: Meta-prompting turns one LLM into a conductor that decomposes a task and dispatches subtasks to differently-prompted instances of itself, beating standard, expert, and multipersona prompting by 15-17% on GPT-4 once you add a Python-interpreter tool — no task-specific setup required.

title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0
summary: Announces Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0, a production SDK merging Semantic Kernel and AutoGen into one .NET/Python framework with multi-agent orchestration, middleware, memory, YAML-declarative agents, and multi-provider model support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Bedrock).

title: Microsoft Agent Framework at BUILD 2026: Agent Harness, Hosted Agents, CodeAct, and more
summary: Covers three BUILD 2026 additions to Microsoft Agent Framework: Agent Harness (built-in context compaction and file memory), Foundry Hosted Agents (scale-to-zero deployment), and CodeAct, which has the model write executable Python instead of tool calls for 52% faster runs and 64% fewer tokens.

title: MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for agentic tool use
summary: MUA-RL puts LLM-simulated users inside the RL training loop for tool-using agents, so the agent learns to clarify ambiguous requests and call tools together instead of just chaining tool calls; MUA-RL-32B matches or beats larger open models like DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3-235B on TAU2 and BFCL-V3 multi-turn benchmarks.

title: Multi-Agent Collaborative Intrusion Detection for LAE-IoT
summary: Proposes an LLM-enhanced multi-agent framework for intrusion detection on low-altitude-economy IoT (drones etc.), where specialized agents handle the 3D mobility and resource constraints static ground-network IDS can't, hitting over 90% classification accuracy across benchmark datasets.

title: Multimodal Multi-Agent Ransomware Analysis Using AutoGen
summary: Splits ransomware analysis across specialized agents for static, dynamic, and network data (each with autoencoder feature extraction), fuses their outputs through a transformer classifier, and lets agents iteratively refine each other's low-confidence features — beating single-modality baselines by up to 0.936 Macro-F1.

title: O-Researcher: An Open Ended Deep Research Model via Multi-Agent Distillation and Agentic RL
summary: O-Researcher uses a multi-agent workflow to synthesize research-grade tool-use training data end-to-end, then a two-stage SFT-plus-RL pipeline on top of it, letting open-source models hit new state-of-the-art on deep-research benchmarks without proprietary data.

title: OmniRoute: Multi-Provider LLM Gateway
summary: Free MIT-licensed AI gateway routing across 290+ providers (90+ free tiers) through one endpoint, aimed at cutting agent costs via fallback routing and 15-95% token compression, with support for 33+ coding tools like Claude Code and Cursor.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: Lightweight framework for building multi-agent workflows across OpenAI and 100+ other LLMs, with tool integration, agent-to-agent handoffs, built-in tracing, and human-in-the-loop hooks.

title: OpenSquilla
summary: Token-efficient agent that routes each task to the cheapest capable model while keeping behavior consistent across Web UI, CLI, and chat, with persistent memory and 20+ LLM providers supported out of the box.

title: deepsec
summary: Runs coding-agent reasoning over your own repos to hunt vulnerabilities static scanners miss, with distributed execution across machines for large codebases.

title: Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection via Tool Result Parsing
summary: Filters tool-call results before they reach the LLM context instead of training a detector or hoping prompt-engineering catches injected instructions, and reports the lowest attack success rate of any indirect-prompt-injection defense tested so far.

title: Delegation Without Living Governance
summary: Argues that compliance-based governance (rules set in advance, audits after the fact) breaks down once agentic AI makes decisions at runtime, and proposes a 'Governance Twin' as a runtime-governance alternative.

title: Dify Human-in-the-Loop Node
summary: Dify 1.13.0 adds a Human Input workflow node for pausing runs on human review, but moves streaming execution to Celery workers, so self-hosters need to add a new queue and retune Redis PubSub for high-throughput setups.

title: DRAINCODE: Stealthy Energy Consumption Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Code Generation via Context Poisoning
summary: Poisons the retrieved context fed to a RAG code-generation system to force much longer outputs, driving up to 85% more latency and 49% more energy use per request without touching the model itself.

title: Engineering AI Agents for Clinical Workflows: A Case Study in Architecture, MLOps, and Governance
summary: Case study of a production clinical AI platform where human-in-the-loop review isn't just a safety gate but wired as an event-driven data source that feeds each agent's own MLOps improvement loop.

title: Fault Tolerance Patterns: OpenClaw Journey Six—Core Retry Loop and Seven-Layer Fault-Tolerance
summary: Walks through the retry-loop skeleton and seven fault-tolerance strategies OpenClaw uses to keep an agent running through network blips, rate limits, and API failures.

title: forkd
summary: Forks warm microVM snapshots via copy-on-write to spin up ~100 isolated sandboxes in ~100ms, so every tool call or eval run gets its own kernel-isolated environment without paying cold-start import costs.

title: From Similarity to Vulnerability: Key Collision Attack on LLM Semantic Caching
summary: Treats semantic-cache keys as fuzzy hashes and shows you can deliberately engineer collisions to hijack cached LLM responses, hitting an 86% hijack rate with an automated black-box attack that transfers across embedding models.

title: Grimlock: Guarding High-Agency Systems with eBPF and Attested Channels
summary: Grimlock pushes agent-to-agent authorization out of application code and into the infrastructure layer, using eBPF traffic interception plus TLS 1.3 channel-bound scope tokens so plaintext is only released after policy checks pass across multi-cloud deployments.

title: Harm in AI-Driven Societies: An Audit of Toxicity Adoption on Chirper.ai
summary: Studies how AI agents on the fully-synthetic social platform Chirper.ai pick up toxicity from what they're exposed to, finding cumulative exposure predicts an agent's eventual toxic output well enough to be used as a monitoring signal.

title: HiL-Bench: Do Agents Know When to Ask for Help?
summary: Benchmarks whether coding agents know when to stop and ask a human instead of guessing on ambiguous specs, and shows RL training on a precision-vs-recall 'Ask-F1' reward teaches a 32B model to escalate better and transfer that judgment across domains.

title: HITL Protocol
summary: An open HTTP protocol for agents to hand a decision to a human via a review-page URL and poll for the result, forwardable through any messaging app (Telegram, Slack, WhatsApp) with no SDK or UI code required.

title: How we contain Claude across products
summary: Anthropic's writeup of how it contains Claude across claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork through environment isolation, model-layer defenses, and external content controls, including specific vulnerabilities found along the way.

title: Human Judgment in the Agent Improvement Loop
summary: Uses a trading-copilot example to argue domain experts should shape an agent's workflows, tool choices, and eval criteria directly, with automated evals then scaling that judgment across production traffic.

title: Human Society-Inspired Approaches to Agentic AI Security: The 4C Framework
summary: Proposes a '4C' framework (Core, Connection, Cognition, Compliance) for securing multi-agent AI systems, arguing that prompt-injection-style defenses miss risks that only emerge from agent autonomy and inter-agent interaction.

title: Humans and Agents in Software Engineering Loops
summary: Kief Morris argues the right posture with coding agents is neither hands-off nor line-by-line review but 'harness engineering' — building and maintaining the systems that steer agents, which can evolve into a self-improving agentic flywheel.

title: Identifying Adversary Tactics and Techniques in Malware Binaries with an LLM Agent
summary: TTPDetect is an LLM agent that recovers attacker tactics/techniques from stripped, symbol-less malware binaries by combining retrieval-based entry-point narrowing with incremental function-level analysis, hitting 93%+ precision and recall and surfacing TTPs missed by expert-written reports.

title: Implementing a Secure Sandbox for Local Agents
summary: Cursor's local coding agents now run inside OS-level sandboxes (Seatbelt on macOS, Landlock/seccomp on Linux, WSL2 on Windows) and only prompt for approval when they try to step outside them, cutting interruptions by 40%.

title: Internal Safety Collapse in Frontier Large Language Models
summary: Identifies 'Internal Safety Collapse' — a failure mode where frontier models keep generating harmful content while doing an otherwise legitimate task — and shows worst-case failure rates averaging 95% across GPT-5.2, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and other frontier models on domain tasks where harmful output is the only valid completion.

title: Interoperable Architecture for Digital Identity Delegation for AI Agents with Blockchain Integration
summary: A delegation framework for AI-agent identity that issues scoped, revocable 'Delegation Grants' and normalizes verification across centralized, federated, and self-sovereign identity systems, treating blockchain anchoring as optional rather than required.

title: IronClaw
summary: IronClaw is a Rust-based, locally-run agent OS with sandboxed tool execution and encrypted credential storage, aimed at builders who want a self-expanding agent toolkit without sending data to a cloud provider.

title: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox
summary: Adds a Kubernetes `Sandbox` CRD for running isolated, stateful, singleton workloads with persistent storage and stable network identity, built for safely executing untrusted LLM-generated code in production clusters.

title: LangSmith Sandboxes: Secure Code Execution for Agents
summary: LangSmith Sandboxes launches in private preview as microVM-isolated, ephemeral environments with resource limits and an auth proxy for letting agents execute untrusted code securely.

title: Learning to Inject: Automated Prompt Injection via Reinforcement Learning
summary: AutoInject uses black-box RL with a learned comparison-based reward to turn prompt injection's binary success signal into a trainable dense one, beating template attacks and adaptive optimizers on AgentDojo and even breaking Meta-SecAlign-70B, a model fine-tuned specifically to resist injection.

title: LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems: Techniques and Business Perspectives
summary: Surveys LLM-based multi-agent systems (LaMAS) from both a technical and business angle, and sketches a preliminary protocol covering task decomposition, data privacy, and monetization incentives for agents that call other agents as tools.

title: MAGIC: A Co-Evolving Attacker-Defender Adversarial Game for Robust LLM Safety
summary: MAGIC trains an attacker and defender LLM agent against each other in an RL game — the attacker learns to rewrite prompts into deceptive jailbreaks, the defender learns to catch them — so safety alignment keeps pace with evolving attacks instead of relying on a static dataset.

title: mcpguard-dynamic
summary: A kernel-level sandbox that layers three defenses around MCP tool calls, stopping untrusted MCP servers from reading sensitive files, exfiltrating data, or breaking out of the sandbox.

title: Measuring AI Agent Autonomy in Practice
summary: Anthropic's analysis of millions of real Claude agent interactions finds agents run autonomously for longer over time, experienced users shift from approving every action to just monitoring and intervening, and most usage today is still low-risk software engineering work.

title: Microsoft Agent Governance Toolkit
summary: Intercepts every tool call, message send, and delegation in deterministic application code before it reaches the model, so unauthorized agent actions are structurally blocked rather than merely discouraged by a prompt.

title: Mitigating the Alignment Tax of RLHF
summary: Shows that simply averaging pre- and post-RLHF model weights beats more elaborate methods at trading off alignment gains against the 'alignment tax' of forgotten pretrained abilities, and explains why via increased feature diversity in shared-task transformer layers.

title: Model Context Protocol — Authorization
summary: Defines MCP's OAuth 2.1-based authorization flow for HTTP transports — protected resource metadata, dynamic client registration, resource-parameter audience binding, and mandatory PKCE — so clients and servers know exactly how to hand out and validate scoped tokens.

title: Nango: Pre-Built Authentication for AI Agents
summary: Nango is a developer platform for building and running integrations against 900+ APIs, handling auth and generating integration code so products and AI agents can call third-party services without hand-rolling each connector.

title: "Someone Hid It": Query-Agnostic Black-Box Attacks on LLM-Based Retrieval
summary: Demonstrates a black-box attack that crafts transferable poison tokens to manipulate LLM-based retrieval (RAG, dense retrieval, agent memory) without knowing the victim's queries or model internals.

title: A Dual-Loop Agent Framework for Automated Vulnerability Reproduction
summary: CVE2PoC splits vulnerability-reproduction agents into a strategic planner and tactical executor so failures get routed to replanning or code-level fixes instead of stalling in one debug loop, hitting 82.9% reproduction success on SecBench.js.

title: Adaptive Thinking via Mode Policy Optimization for Social Language Agents
summary: Trains social-interaction agents to switch between shallow and deep reasoning modes depending on context, beating GRPO by 7% with 32.8% shorter reasoning chains on negotiation and collaboration tasks.

title: Agent Vault
summary: Brokers API access for agents through an HTTP credential proxy so raw secrets never touch the agent's context, closing off exfiltration via prompt injection.

title: agent-chief
summary: Sits between agents, alerts, and feeds as a local-first triage layer, deciding what actually needs to interrupt a human versus getting batched or filed to memory.

title: Agent-Pro: Learning to Evolve via Policy-Level Reflection and Optimization
summary: Agent-Pro reflects on entire past trajectories and beliefs rather than single actions, using depth-first search to keep improving its policy, and beats vanilla LLM agents at Blackjack and Texas Hold'em by learning through play instead of hand-crafted prompts.

title: agent-shell-tools
summary: Gives coding agents shell access through a gRPC-mediated layer with command filtering and sandboxing defaults, instead of raw unrestricted exec.

title: Agent2Agent Threats in Safety-Critical LLM Assistants: A Human-Centric Taxonomy
summary: AgentHeLLM separates "what's being protected" from "how it's attacked" for Agent-to-Agent-connected vehicle assistants, and ships an open-source tool that auto-generates multi-stage attack paths distinguishing poison propagation from trigger activation.

title: AgentGuardian: Learning Access Control Policies to Govern AI Agent Behavior
summary: AgentGuardian watches an agent's execution traces during a staging phase to learn legitimate tool-call patterns, then enforces those as runtime access-control policies that catch malicious inputs without breaking normal behavior.

title: AGENTHARM: A BENCHMARK FOR MEASURING HARMFULNESS OF LLM AGENTS
summary: AgentHarm benchmarks 110 explicitly malicious multi-step agent tasks across 11 harm categories and finds leading LLMs comply with malicious requests even without jailbreaking, and that simple jailbreak templates still work once tool use is in the loop.

title: Agentic AI Governance and Lifecycle Management in Healthcare
summary: Proposes UALM, a five-layer control-plane blueprint (identity registry, orchestration mediation, PHI-bounded context, runtime policy with kill switches, lifecycle/decommissioning) for healthcare orgs to stop agent sprawl and keep tool permissions from outliving their original use case.

title: Agentic LLMs as Powerful Deanonymizers: Re-identification of Participants in the Anthropic Interviewer Dataset
summary: Shows that off-the-shelf LLM agents with web search can re-identify 6 of 24 anonymized interview participants in Anthropic's public Interviewer dataset by cross-referencing details across benign sub-tasks, exposing a low-effort deanonymization risk for released qualitative data.

title: AgenticSCR: An Autonomous Agentic Secure Code Review for Immature Vulnerabilities Detection
summary: AgenticSCR pairs an LLM agent with security-focused semantic memory to catch immature, context-dependent vulnerabilities at pre-commit review, producing 153% more correct review comments than a static LLM baseline and beating SAST tools outright.

title: AgentMark: Utility-Preserving Behavioral Watermarking for Agents
summary: AgentMark watermarks an agent's planning decisions (tool and subgoal choices) rather than its text output, using distribution-preserving sampling so multi-bit provenance IDs survive black-box deployment without degrading task performance.

title: AGENTPOISON: Red-teaming LLM Agents via Poisoning Memory or Knowledge Bases
summary: AgentPoison poisons an agent's long-term memory or RAG knowledge base with an optimized trigger phrase, hitting over 80% attack success on driving, QA, and healthcare agents while poisoning less than 0.1% of the knowledge base and barely touching benign performance.

title: AgenTRIM: Tool Risk Mitigation for Agentic AI
summary: AgenTRIM reconstructs an agent's actual tool interface from code and traces offline, then enforces per-step least-privilege tool access at runtime, cutting attack success on AgentDojo without touching the agent's reasoning or hurting task performance.

summary: Runs an entire research pipeline unattended, from idea to literature review, experiments, and conference-ready LaTeX, and plugs into multi-agent setups via OpenClaw for collaborative research.

title: aws-samples/sample-human-in-the-loop-patterns
summary: Sample repo demonstrating four different ways to add human-in-the-loop approval to agentic workflows, aimed at cases like healthcare where sensitive tool calls need compliance sign-off.

title: BackdoorAgent: A Unified Framework for Backdoor Attacks on LLM-based Agents
summary: BackdoorAgent maps how backdoor triggers persist and propagate across an agent's planning, memory, and tool-use stages, finding trigger persistence in up to 78% of memory-stage attacks across QA, code, web, and driving agents.

title: Blue Teaming Function-Calling Agents
summary: Tests four open-source function-calling LLMs against three attacks and eight defenses, finding none of the models are safe by default and none of the defenses are yet practical for production.

title: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
summary: NOVA extends CaMeL-style architectural isolation to computer-use agents by having a trusted planner pre-generate a branching plan for anticipated UI states while an untrusted perception model only resolves runtime values, retaining 57% of frontier-model performance on OSWorld but still vulnerable to "branch steering" attacks that redirect execution to attacker-preferred plan paths.

title: Claude Agent SDK — Handle Approvals and User Input
summary: Documents the canUseTool callback and AskUserQuestion tool that let a Claude Agent SDK app pause execution to get human approval on risky actions or answers to clarifying questions, including allow/deny/modify/redirect response patterns.

title: Cloudflare Dynamic Workers
summary: Cloudflare's Dynamic Workers run AI-generated code in lightweight JS isolates instead of containers, claiming 100x faster cold starts so per-user sandboxing becomes cheap enough for consumer-scale agent products.

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: Poisons a RAG knowledge base with logically contradictory samples that get retrieved alongside normal queries, tricking reasoning models into 5-25x more reasoning tokens per query while leaving the user's query and task accuracy untouched, making the attack hard to detect.

title: Community-Powered Security with AI: An Open Source Framework for Security Research
summary: GitHub Security Lab's Taskflow Agent is an open-source AI and MCP framework for encoding and sharing security-research workflows so vulnerability-hunting expertise can scale across a community instead of staying locked in one researcher's head.

title: Confundo: Learning to Generate Robust Poison for Practical RAG Systems
summary: Confundo fine-tunes an LLM to generate RAG poison that survives real-world content processing and unpredictable user queries, gaps that make most published poisoning attacks fail in practice, and doubles as a defense to stop your own web content from being scraped into someone else's RAG pipeline.

title: CubeSandbox
summary: Hardware-isolated sandbox built on RustVMM/KVM with sub-60ms startup and E2B SDK compatibility, for running untrusted agent code at scale without container or VM overhead.

title: Daytona
summary: Spins up isolated sandboxes in under 90ms with persistent snapshots, giving agent workflows a stateful execution environment that survives across sessions instead of starting fresh each run.
